ai.title: backend/deploy.sh drops latest tag, pushes timestamped image
ai.summary: backend/deploy.sh removes the :latest Docker tag from build and push steps, now only tagging and pushing gcr.io/$GCP_PROJECT/$VM_NAME:$TIMESTAMP. This ensures each deploy is uniquely identified by timestamp rather than overwriting a mutable latest pointer. Scope limited to backend/deploy.sh. The commented-out push for the timestamped tag is now active.

eli5.text: When the team deploys a new version of the backend service, the system no longer labels and uploads a shared 'latest' copy that gets overwritten on every release. Instead, it tags and pushes each deployment with a unique timestamp, so every version is preserved separately and can be traced back to when it was built. You would only notice this if you manage or inspect the deployment process: the shared 'latest' reference is gone, and each deploy now carries its own time-based label. This affects whoever runs or tracks deployments of the backend service.

ai.title: Suppress websocket ping errors in realtime client
ai.summary: Ping websocket errors are no longer printed from the shared realtime client. `APIRealtimeClient` heartbeat calls `sendMessage('ping', {})` every 30000 ms and now swallows rejected pings instead of `console.error`. The change is limited to `common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts`. Existing heartbeat timing and connection behavior remain unchanged.

eli5.text: Every 30 seconds, the app quietly checks whether its connection to the server is still alive by sending a small 'ping' message. If that ping failed, the app used to print an error message on the screen. Now, those failed pings are silently ignored so you no longer see those error messages cluttering your view. This only affects how failed connection checks are handled; the frequency and mechanics of the checks remain exactly as before.
